nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $E_n$ is the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, with coordinates indexed by $0, \dots, 2n-1$ and the standard inner product.
nodes.title: The model space $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ of the Liouville–Arnold theorem

nodes.summary: For $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the coordinate $p_i$ of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is coordinate number $i$: this map sends $i$ to the same number $i$, regarded as an index in $\{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Liouville–Arnold coordinates: index of $p_i$

nodes.summary: For $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the coordinate $q_i$ of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is coordinate number $n + i$: this map sends $i$ to $n + i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Liouville–Arnold coordinates: index of $q_i$

nodes.summary: Functions $F_0, \dots, F_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}$ are Liouville integrable on a set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ if each $F_i$ is $C^\infty$ on $U$, the Poisson brackets $\{F_i, F_j\}$ vanish at every point of $U$ for all $i, j$, and at every $x \in U$ the Fréchet derivatives $dF_0(x), \dots, dF_{n-1}(x)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Liouville integrable system on a subset of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$

nodes.summary: For functions $F_0, \dots, F_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}$ and values $c_0, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \mathbb{R}$, the common level set is $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^{2n} : F_i(x) = c_i \text{ for all } i\}$.
nodes.title: Common level set of $n$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be open and let $F_0, \dots, F_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}$ be Liouville integrable on $U$. For $c = (c_0, \dots, c_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, let $M_c = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^{2n} : F_i(x) = c_i \text{ for all } i\}$ be the common level set. If $M_c \subseteq U$ and $M_c$ is compact and connected (in particular nonempty), then $M_c$ is homeomorphic to the $n$-torus…
nodes.title: Liouville–Arnold theorem

nodes.summary: Write the coordinates of a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ as $p_i = x_i$ and $q_i = x_{n+i}$ for $i = 0, \dots, n-1$. For functions $F, G \colon \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}$, the Poisson bracket for the symplectic form $\omega_0 = \sum_i dp_i \wedge dq_i$ is the function
nodes.title: Standard Poisson bracket on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
